investment_summary:
Moody's combined 9% revenue growth with margin expansion in 2025, lifting operating margin to 43.4% and diluted EPS 21% to $13.67 [1]. Free cash flow reached $2.58 billion, and total debt fell to $7.35 billion [1].

Consensus rates the stock Buy, with a $553.67 target and FY2026 EPS of $16.76 [3]. These figures are dated 2026-11-25, after the 10-K. Consensus expects FY2026 revenue growth of only 6.5% [3]. The reverse DCF implies 18.1% annual growth for ten years, against a 12.2% historical three-year CAGR [2][3]. On that path the implied return is 6.1%, below an 11.3% WACC. The current valuation therefore requires growth well above both consensus and recent history.

The main risks are debt-issuance cyclicality, litigation exposure and AI-driven competition [1]. Shareholder payouts absorbed about 94% of free cash flow [1].
key_takeaways: Margin expansion should continue as cost growth stays below revenue growth: operating margin reached 43.4% from 40.6% [1].
The current price looks demanding: the enterprise value implies 18.1% annual growth versus 6.5% consensus, so upside needs acceleration [2][3].
Deleveraging should persist, but payouts near 94% of free cash flow leave little room for further debt reduction [1].
Issuance cyclicality is the main earnings risk, since most credit-rating revenue is transaction-based and tied to debt volumes [1].
business_overview:
Moody's Corporation is a global integrated risk assessment firm. It provides credit ratings, research, proprietary data, analytical models and cloud-based decision tools to banks, insurers, investors, corporations and governments [1]. The company reports two segments: Moody's Analytics (MA), with external revenue of $3,599 million, and Moody's Investors Service (MIS), with $4,119 million [1]. Total 2025 revenue was $7,718 million, up 9% from $7,088 million, and the company employs about 16,000 people in more than 40 countries [1]. U.S. revenue was $4,171 million, or 54% of the total, and EMEA contributed $2,376 million [1].

MA growth is led by Decision Solutions, where revenue rose 12% to $1,692 million. Insurance grew 15% to $685 million and KYC grew 19% to $438 million [1]. Banking grew only 3% to $569 million, because transaction revenue fell 18% as MA moved toward cloud-hosted subscriptions [1]. Research and Insights grew 7% to $995 million, and Data and Information grew 7% to $912 million [1]. Total MA annual recurring revenue (ARR) reached $3,498 million, up 8% at year-end [1].

MIS is driven by debt issuance. Corporate Finance (CFG) revenue rose 9% to $2,132 million, helped by $144 million of transaction revenue from higher investment-grade and high-yield issuance [1]. Public, Project and Infrastructure Finance grew 13% to $635 million, the fastest MIS line, while Structured Finance grew 8% to $558 million and Financial Institutions grew 4% to $759 million [1]. The MIS adjusted operating margin reached 63.6% [1].

Recent initiatives include the acquisitions of Praedicat, Numerated, CAPE Analytics and ICR Chile, and the sale of MA Learning Solutions for a $23 million gain [1]. A $108 million restructuring program ran in 2025, and in October 2025 the board authorized $4.0 billion of share repurchases [1]. Management points to generative and agentic AI, private credit and rising debt issuance as growth opportunities [1].
market_position:
The 10-K does not disclose market share, so Moody's position has to be judged from its economics and competitive set [1]. MIS competes with other credit rating agencies, investment banks and brokerages, while MA competes with diversified financial information and enterprise risk software providers [1]. On that basis Moody's is best classified as an established market leader rather than a challenger: its MIS adjusted operating margin of 63.6% and group adjusted margin of 51.1% are high, and the filing cites its brand as a key competitive strength [1].

Customers are concentrated in banks, insurers and other financial institutions, particularly for MA's sanctions, KYC and insurance products [1]. The filing gives no customer concentration figures, so dependence on the largest clients cannot be measured. The geographic mix is more visible: about 39% of 2025 revenue was non-U.S. dollar, and EMEA is the largest international region at $2,376 million [1]. This provides some diversification but also adds foreign-exchange exposure.

Structural pressures are visible in the filing. Issuers increasingly select unrated securities, ratings from financial advisers, or non-bank lending that requires no rating, which would shrink the pool of rated issues [1]. New regulation, including the EU ESG Rating Regulation applicable from July 2026, could also reshape the market for rated products [1]. Growth therefore depends on MA's shift to subscriptions continuing to offset transaction softness in banking [1].
operating_results:
Revenue rose 9% to $7,718 million, and organic constant-currency growth was 7% [1]. MA and MIS external revenue each grew 9% [1]. Cost of revenue rose only 1%, so gross margin rose to 74.4% from 72.6% [1]. Operating and SG&A expense grew 3%, but restructuring charges rose 83% to $108 million [1]. Operating margin reached 43.4% from 40.6%, and net margin also improved [1].

Diluted EPS rose 21% to $13.67 [1]. The effective tax rate fell because of a 2025 tax benefit, although management says a $221 million net non-operating expense offsets that benefit, so EPS is unaffected [1]. On an adjusted basis, diluted EPS rose 20% to $14.94 and adjusted operating margin expanded 300 basis points to 51.1% [1]. Operating cash flow rose $63 million to $2.90 billion and free cash flow rose $54 million to $2.58 billion, held back by $212 million of higher tax payments [1].

Segment profit shows the same pattern. MA adjusted operating income rose 18% to $1,196 million, with margin up 240 basis points to 33.1%, even though MA restructuring charges rose to $77 million [1]. MIS adjusted operating income rose 15% to $2,746 million, with margin up 350 basis points to 63.6%, as operating and SG&A expense fell 1% [1]. Over 2022 to 2025 revenue compounded at roughly 12% a year, from $5,468 million to $7,718 million [1][4].
risk_assessment:
The filing identifies three principal risks: regulatory and litigation exposure, dependence on debt-issuance volumes, and competitive and technological disruption, including generative AI and free information [1]. Regulation weighs most heavily on MIS, which is subject to formal inspections in the EU, UK, Australia, Singapore, Japan and Hong Kong, and to direct SEC oversight [1]. Legal exposure rises in downturns: the filing says investigations and proceedings increased significantly after the 2007 to 2008 financial crisis [1]. Moody's also states it may not have adequate insurance or reserves to cover these risks [1].

Issuance dependence is the most cyclical exposure. The filing states that a majority of credit-rating revenue is transaction-based and depends on the number and dollar volume of debt securities issued [1]. Fixed costs in rent, technology, compliance and compensation are hard to reduce in the short term, so a fall in issuance hits operating profit quickly [1]. New EU rules add cost: the ESG Rating Regulation applies from July 2026, and the EU AI Act brings compliance costs and possible fines [1].

Balance-sheet risk sits in acquired intangibles. Goodwill of $6,368 million and intangibles of $1,866 million total $8,234 million, about 52% of assets, and tangible book value is negative at -$4.18 billion [1]. The filing attributes about 94% of these balances to MA, so any impairment would most likely come from MA if its projections are missed [1]. Quality scores from [2] are mixed: the Altman Z-score is 7.26, in the safe zone, though that model is designed for manufacturers. The Piotroski F-score is 7 of 8, and the one failed test is a leverage measure that should be checked against the falling debt balance [2].
competitors_analysis:
Peers were chosen for business model first and size second. S&P Global (SPGI) is the closest, with data, analytics and benchmarks at similar scale [4]. MSCI (MSCI) is next, with subscription-based research, analytics and index data that carries a comparable recurring-revenue profile [4]. Morningstar (MORN) is third, a subscription data and research provider that is much smaller, at $2.6 billion of revenue [4]. FICO was excluded because its scores business is a different model.

On growth and margins, Moody's 2025 revenue growth of 8.9% was second behind MSCI at 9.7%, and ahead of SPGI at 7.9% and MORN at 7.5% [4]. Its EBITDA margin of 50.4% was level with SPGI at 50.2%, well below MSCI at 61.3%, and far above MORN at 29.7% [4]. Its gross margin of 74.4% trails only MSCI, which sits near 82%, and stays 3.3 to 4.6 points above SPGI in every year [4].

On returns and valuation, Moody's ROIC of 24.3% is second to MSCI at 38.7%, and well ahead of MORN at 17.6% and SPGI at 11.4% [4]. Its EV/EBITDA of 24.59x sits near MSCI at 24.97x and above the peer median of 20.74x [4]. Consensus rates the stock Buy with a $553.67 target, and forward P/E is 29.0x on FY2026 EPS, both dated after the 10-K [3]. Cash conversion is the weak point: the reported FCF conversion of 1.05 is the lowest in the group, against 1.18 to 1.22 for peers [4]. That ratio does not match a simple division of free cash flow of $2,575 million by EBITDA of $3,891 million, which implies a much lower figure, so the definition must be confirmed [4]. Returns support part of the premium, but the premium is not fully justified until cash conversion recovers.

investment_theses.thesis: Operating leverage keeps margins expanding, because operating and SG&A cost growth stays well below revenue growth.
investment_theses.evidence: Operating margin rose to 43.4% from 40.6% and gross margin to 74.4%; cost of revenue rose only 1% while revenue grew 9%, and operating and SG&A grew only 3% [1]. MIS adjusted operating margin reached 63.6% [1].
investment_theses.signpost: FY2026 operating margin above 43.4% in the FY2026 10-K (filed about February 2027).
investment_theses.invalidation: FY2026 operating margin below 40.6%, or restructuring charges rising again without a matching margin gain.

investment_theses.thesis: The share price assumes growth well above consensus, so at consensus growth the implied return falls short of the cost of capital.
investment_theses.evidence: The reverse DCF implies 18.1% annual revenue growth for ten years, against 6.5% FY2026 and 6.7% FY2027 consensus growth and a 12.2% historical three-year CAGR [2][3]. The implied IRR is 6.1% against an 11.3% WACC [2][3]. Consensus data is dated 2026-11-25, after the 10-K.
investment_theses.signpost: FY2026 revenue growth of at least 9%, matching the FY2025 pace, reported in the FY2026 10-K (about February 2027).
investment_theses.invalidation: FY2026 revenue growth of 12% or more, which would show growth can outpace consensus and justify the implied path.

investment_theses.thesis: Deleveraging continues, but payouts near 94% of free cash flow will limit further debt reduction.
investment_theses.evidence: Total debt fell to $7.35 billion from $7.75 billion, and debt to equity to 1.81x from 2.17x [1]. Buybacks of $1.71 billion and dividends of $701 million absorbed about 94% of $2.58 billion free cash flow [1].
investment_theses.signpost: FY2026 total debt below $7.35 billion, with buybacks plus dividends at or below free cash flow, in the FY2026 10-K.
investment_theses.invalidation: Total debt rising above $7.35 billion, or payouts exceeding free cash flow for a second consecutive year.

investment_theses.thesis: Debt-issuance cyclicality will show up in MIS earnings within a year, so the stock is exposed to a weaker issuance cycle.
investment_theses.evidence: A majority of credit-rating revenue is transaction-based and depends on debt issuance volumes [1]. Corporate Finance transaction revenue added $144 million in 2025 [1]. Diluted EPS for the quarter to September 2026 was $4.14 against a $4.25 estimate, a 2.5% miss [3].
investment_theses.signpost: Corporate Finance (CFG) revenue growth of at least 5% in FY2026, against 9% in FY2025, reported in the FY2026 10-K.
investment_theses.invalidation: CFG revenue growth stays at or above 9% in FY2026 even if debt issuance volumes are flat.
